chunks.text: 69-year-old female, Service or Sales Worker, resident of Woodlands, Singapore.
General Anesthesia with Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA)

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Kumar, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery today. I just want to go over a few things to make sure we're all set for your laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia with an LMA.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Good morning, doctor. I'm ready, just want to get this done and feel better.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Can you tell me a bit about your medical history and how you've been feeling lately?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I've had gallstones for a while now, and the doctor said surgery is the best way to go. I also have high blood pressure, diabetes, and my BMI is a bit high. Oh, and my kidney function is a little off, but it's stable.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Let's go through your medications. I see here that you're on Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, Insulin Glargine, and Ranitidine. Can you confirm if you're still taking all of these, or have any been changed or stopped?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Most of them are still the same, doctor. I take Metformin 500mg twice a day, Lisinopril 10mg once a day, Atorvastatin 20mg once a day, and Insulin Glargine 30 units once at night. But I stopped the Ranitidine about six months ago because the doctor said my peptic ulcer had healed and I didn't need it anymore.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for clarifying that. It's important we have the most up-to-date medication list. Do you have any allergies? I see penicillin listed with a rash.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I had a rash when I took penicillin before, so I avoid that. No other drug allergies that I know of.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? Any issues like waking up during surgery, difficult intubation, or nausea afterward?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first surgery. I've never had anesthesia before, so I'm a bit nervous about that.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's completely normal. We'll make sure you're comfortable and safe throughout. Are you NPO since midnight? Nothing by mouth after 8 PM?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I haven't had anything to eat or drink since last night. Just a sip of water with my morning insulin, but that was hours ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. And how would you describe your overall energy level and ability to perform daily activities?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can still walk and do my daily tasks, but I do get a bit tired, especially after meals. But I manage okay lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for that information. We'll make sure to tailor your anesthesia plan to your needs. You'll be asleep during the surgery, and we'll use a laryngeal mask airway to help you breathe. You'll have a tube in your throat only if needed, but we'll try to avoid that if possible.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Alright, that sounds good. I trust you, doctor.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Tan. We'll be with you every step of the way. I'll see you in the operating room shortly. Any last questions?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] LMA size four inserted, good seal, capnography confirmed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] 18-gauge IV in right antecubital fossa, 500 mils of Ringer's lactate bolused

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty five, gave phenylephrine ten micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] surgery completed, LMA removed, patient extubated smoothly

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm feeling a bit tired, but okay. Got some pain in the tummy area.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Can you rate the pain for me, from 0 to 10? And have you felt nauseous at all?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe a 4 or 5? And yeah, a little bit of nausea, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, we can manage that pain and nausea for you. How’s your breathing? Any discomfort or difficulty breathing?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine, no problem. Throat is a bit sore though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That sore throat can happen from the LMA tube. It should ease soon. Any moments where you felt awake during the surgery or remember anything?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don’t remember anything. Went to sleep and woke up here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Given your diabetes, kidney issues, and high blood pressure, we’ll keep a close eye on your vitals and fluid balance. Any other concerns?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that’s all for now. Thanks for checking on me.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Of course. We’ll get you more comfortable and ready to move to the ward soon.
